title: What are x and y in these two figures?
description: In the first figure a right angle is split into sixty five degrees and x, and y makes a linear pair with x. In the second figure two lines make two angles with a lower line, and x is the angle between them. A closing check adds each answer to its partner.
teaching_notes: One idea: a part is found by taking the other part away from the whole, whether the whole is a right angle, a straight line or a larger angle. Watch for students who add the two angles in the second figure instead of taking one away.

video_script.why: The child uses a right angle, a linear pair and a split angle, as in the solved example, to find x and y in two figures.
video_script.substitution: the book's own two figures: parallel lines with a transversal and a right angle split into sixty five degrees and x, and two lines meeting a lower line at seventy eight degrees and fifty three degrees
video_script.anchor: two small figures: the first with parallel lines, a transversal and a right angle split into 65° and x, with y beside x; the second with two lines above a lower line making 78° and 53° with it
video_script.payoff_line: Every angle came from taking a part away from a whole

final_answer.spoken: in the first figure, x is twenty five degrees and y is one hundred and fifty five degrees, and in the second figure, x is twenty five degrees

maths_rules: x and 65 fill a right angle, so x = 90 - 65 = 25
y and x are a linear pair, so y = 180 - 25 = 155
in the second figure the two lines make 78 and 53 with the lower line, so x = 78 - 53 = 25
video_script.design: Two small figures side by side. The part that is found takes one colour, the part that is given takes another, and the whole is marked above them.
